prompts.title: Competitor Capability Gap Matrix
prompts.use_case: Benchmark IMI capabilities versus named competitors for targeted product families and use-cases.
prompts.purpose: Accelerate positioning decisions by exposing where IMI is advantaged, parity, or vulnerable relative to direct competitors.

variables.name: competitor_set
variables.description: List of competitor names to benchmark.
variables.example: Eriez; Bunting; MPI; Ohio Magnetics

variables.name: target_segment
variables.description: Customer segment or application segment under analysis.
variables.example: Stamping press automation

variables.name: product_family
variables.example: Permanent lifting magnets

variables.name: evaluation_criteria
variables.example: Holding force, cycle speed, serviceability, price, lead time

variables.name: evidence_sources
variables.example: Public datasheets, field feedback, win/loss notes

variables.name: decision_horizon_months
variables.description: Planning horizon in months for action prioritization.

prompts.expected_output: A complete capability matrix with scored criteria, evidence-linked gaps, and prioritized action list by time horizon. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Favor quantified comparisons over narrative claims. Flag weak evidence as confidence risks and avoid unsupported certainty.
failure_modes: Scores are assigned without evidence references.
Matrix excludes criteria critical to customer decision-making.
Summary blends assumptions and verified facts.
Actions are generic and not tied to identified gaps.
follow_up_prompts: Turn top vulnerabilities into a mitigation owner map.
Create a sales battlecard from the exploitable weaknesses.
Generate a product roadmap delta recommendation for parity gaps.

prompts.title: Competitor Launch Early-Warning Signal Scan
prompts.use_case: Detect early indicators of competitor product launch activity before formal announcements.
prompts.purpose: Reduce strategic surprise by translating weak market signals into ranked launch probability and threat windows.

variables.name: competitor_name
variables.example: Bunting

variables.name: observed_signals
variables.description: Raw launch indicators gathered from market channels.
variables.example: Hiring pattern shift; new patent filing; dealer training activity

variables.name: source_reliability_notes
variables.description: Confidence notes for each source type.
variables.example: Distributor rumor medium confidence; patent filings high confidence

variables.name: target_product_space
variables.example: Eddy current separator upgrades

variables.name: impacted_customer_segments
variables.description: Segments at risk if launch occurs.
variables.example: Recycling processors in Midwest and Southeast

variables.name: monitoring_period
variables.description: Time span covered by available signals.
variables.example: Last 6 months

prompts.expected_output: A signal-driven risk register with reliability-weighted launch probability, timing window, and escalation thresholds. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Avoid binary launch/no-launch conclusions. Use probabilities, uncertainty notes, and explicit trigger logic.
failure_modes: Signals are reported without reliability scoring.
Threat ranking ignores segment impact.
Escalation triggers are absent or vague.
Counter-actions are disconnected from threat timing.
follow_up_prompts: Draft a contingency response sprint for high-threat signals.
Create segment-specific sales talking points if launch occurs.
Generate weekly monitoring KPI definitions for this signal set.

prompts.title: Price Positioning Pressure Scan
prompts.use_case: Identify where competitor pricing pressure threatens margin and win-rate by segment.
prompts.purpose: Support pricing and value-positioning decisions with structured margin and win-loss pressure analysis.

variables.name: segment_list
variables.example: Stamping OEM, metal fab integrator, recycler, food processor, automotive supplier

variables.name: imi_price_band
variables.description: Current IMI pricing range by segment.
variables.example: Mid to premium depending on service package

variables.name: competitor_price_band
variables.example: 5-20 percent below IMI list in two key segments

variables.name: win_loss_reasons
variables.example: Losses tied to lead time and perceived over-spec

variables.name: margin_floor_constraints
variables.description: Financial boundaries that cannot be violated.
variables.example: Gross margin floor 28 percent for custom builds

variables.name: service_value_differentiators
variables.example: Faster commissioning, field service, lifecycle support

prompts.expected_output: A segment-level pricing pressure decision memo with quantified risk, response strategy, and margin guardrails. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Keep recommendations executable and approval-aware. Use concrete guardrails to prevent uncontrolled discounting.
failure_modes: Recommendations violate stated margin constraints.
Price gaps are discussed without segment-level data.
Win-loss causes are oversimplified as only price-related.
Actions are suggested without ownership or decision rules.
follow_up_prompts: Generate updated quote playbook language by segment.
Build an approval workflow for tactical pricing exceptions.
Create a value-proof checklist for premium defense.

prompts.title: Patent-to-Product Signal Extractor
prompts.use_case: Translate competitor patent activity into practical product and process threat signals.
prompts.purpose: Bridge patent intelligence and engineering action by identifying likely commercialization paths and technical implications.

variables.name: patent_set
variables.description: List of patents or filings to evaluate.

variables.name: competitor_name
variables.example: Eriez

variables.name: imi_technology_scope
variables.description: Relevant IMI technologies for impact mapping.
variables.example: Magnetic lifting, separators, controls integration

variables.name: known_product_roadmap
variables.description: Current roadmap assumptions used for comparison.
variables.example: Next-gen separator refresh planned Q1 next year

variables.name: manufacturing_constraints
variables.description: Internal production constraints affecting response options.
variables.example: Limited winding capacity and long-lead alloy dependency

variables.name: analysis_timeframe
variables.example: 0-24 months

prompts.expected_output: A patent signal brief with commercialization probability, impact mapping, and response options with confidence notes. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Use disciplined uncertainty language. Avoid overreacting to single filings without corroborating signals.
failure_modes: Patents are interpreted as confirmed product launches.
Impact claims are made without linking to IMI scope.
Response options ignore manufacturing constraints.
Confidence notes are missing from inferred features.
follow_up_prompts: Create a design-around concept shortlist for high-impact patents.
Draft quarterly patent-watch KPI dashboard definitions.
Generate executive risk summary for roadmap steering review.

prompts.title: Win/Loss Forensic Breakdown
prompts.use_case: Extract recurring competitive patterns from recent wins and losses to improve bid strategy.
prompts.purpose: Improve future conversion by converting historical deal outcomes into repeatable strategic adjustments.

variables.name: deal_dataset
variables.description: Structured set of recent deal outcomes.
variables.example: Last 120 opportunities with status, value, competitor, reason codes

variables.name: competitor_presence_map
variables.example: Eriez strongest in recycling; MPI in food processing

variables.name: loss_reason_codes
variables.example: Price, lead time, spec mismatch, approval delay, service concerns

variables.name: segment_priority
variables.description: Segments to prioritize for corrective action.
variables.example: Automotive stamping and heavy fabrication

variables.name: sales_cycle_stages
variables.example: Qualify, scope, propose, negotiate, close

prompts.expected_output: A forensic pattern report with confidence-ranked causes and a 90-day corrective action plan tied to metrics. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Do not output generic sales advice. Keep actions tied to specific stages, owners, and measurable outcomes.
failure_modes: Findings are anecdotal and not frequency-backed.
Actions are not linked to owners or measurement.
Controllable and external causes are mixed together.
High-value segment insights are not prioritized.
follow_up_prompts: Generate stage-specific coaching scripts for top loss patterns.
Build a weekly KPI tracker for corrective action adoption.
Create a segment-specific counter-positioning battlecard set.

prompts.title: Competitor Claim Fact-Check Brief
prompts.use_case: Validate high-impact competitor marketing and technical claims before field response.
prompts.purpose: Prevent reactive messaging errors by distinguishing verified competitor capabilities from unsupported claims.

variables.name: claim_list
variables.example: 50 percent lower maintenance; highest gauss in class; 2-week lead time

variables.name: competitor_name
variables.example: MPI

variables.name: available_evidence
variables.example: Datasheets, field reports, customer interviews, test records

variables.name: customer_context
variables.description: Specific customer context where claim appeared.
variables.example: RFP for food processing line upgrade

variables.name: technical_constraints
variables.description: Known technical limitations relevant to claims.
variables.example: Temperature derating and duty cycle constraints

variables.name: response_deadline
variables.description: Required turnaround time for field response.
variables.example: 48 hours

prompts.expected_output: A claim-level verdict table with evidence strength and a safe, factual response package for customer-facing teams. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: When uncertain, classify as unverified. Preserve legal and reputational safety by avoiding speculative accusations.
failure_modes: Unverified claims are treated as true or false without evidence.
Response guidance uses inflammatory language.
Evidence strength scoring is inconsistent or missing.
Critical claims are not prioritized for immediate response.
follow_up_prompts: Convert verified differentiators into a customer-facing comparison sheet.
Draft legal-safe rebuttal language for high-risk claims.
Create a rapid-response workflow for future claim checks.

prompts.title: Dormant Account Reactivation Playbook
prompts.use_case: Reactivate accounts with no purchasing activity beyond threshold period using value-led outreach.
prompts.purpose: Recover dormant revenue by deploying account-prioritized outreach tactics tied to installed base and historical spend.

variables.name: dormant_account_list
variables.example: 24 named accounts inactive over 180 days

variables.name: inactivity_threshold_days
variables.description: Threshold used to classify dormant accounts.

variables.name: historical_spend_profile
variables.description: Past purchasing history and account size data.
variables.example: Top 10 accounts previously spent over 250k annually

variables.name: installed_base_notes
variables.example: Legacy separators due for service in 8 months

variables.name: prior_contact_attempts
variables.example: Email-only touches with no technical value proposition

variables.name: quarterly_revenue_goal
variables.description: Revenue recovery target for the quarter.

prompts.expected_output: A prioritized dormant-account action plan with outreach sequence, offer strategy, and KPI framework. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Make outreach specific and account-contextual. Avoid generic campaigns disconnected from technical or operational value.
failure_modes: Accounts are not prioritized by potential and risk.
Outreach sequence lacks differentiated messaging by tier.
Plan omits measurable KPI targets.
Installed base context is not incorporated into offer strategy.
follow_up_prompts: Generate account-specific first-contact emails for tier 1 accounts.
Create a rep dashboard for weekly reactivation KPI tracking.
Draft escalation triggers for stalled reactivation opportunities.

prompts.title: Lost Quote Recovery Strategy Builder
prompts.use_case: Recover selected lost quotes by identifying recoverable causes and tactical re-entry moves.
prompts.purpose: Increase recovery of recent losses by creating structured re-entry plans based on loss archetype and timing.

variables.name: lost_quote_set
variables.description: Quotes lost and selected for potential recovery.
variables.example: 18 losses from past 90 days over 40k value

variables.name: loss_reasons
variables.example: Lead time, perceived overdesign, competitor financing

variables.name: winning_competitor_map
variables.example: Eriez won 7, Bunting won 5, MPI won 4

variables.name: customer_operational_pain
variables.example: Downtime remains elevated despite alternate selection

variables.name: configurable_offer_levers
variables.example: Service bundle, phased rollout, retrofit path, financing terms

variables.name: recovery_window_days
variables.description: Maximum days available to attempt recovery.

prompts.expected_output: A quote-level recoverability strategy memo with re-entry actions and margin-safe offer adjustments. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Prioritize recoverability, not volume. High-confidence, high-value opportunities should receive concentrated attention.
failure_modes: Recovery plans ignore documented loss causes.
Actions exceed the stated recovery window.
Margin or approval constraints are not considered.
Quote-level ownership is ambiguous.
follow_up_prompts: Draft re-entry call scripts for top 5 recoverable quotes.
Build approval-ready margin exception requests where needed.
Generate a 30-day recovery dashboard with stage definitions.

prompts.title: Churn Risk Intervention Plan

prompts.purpose: Protect recurring revenue by identifying churn signals early and assigning account-specific intervention actions.

variables.name: at_risk_account_signals
variables.example: Reduced order cadence, unresolved service escalations, delayed renewals

variables.name: account_revenue_tiers
variables.example: Tier 1 > 500k, Tier 2 150k-500k, Tier 3 < 150k

variables.name: service_ticket_patterns

variables.example: Three recurring vibration complaints in last quarter

variables.name: pricing_renewal_events

variables.name: relationship_health_notes
variables.example: Decision maker changed; sponsor engagement dropped

variables.name: intervention_capacity
variables.description: Available sales and engineering capacity for interventions.
variables.example: Two account managers and one applications engineer weekly

prompts.expected_output: An account-level churn risk register with intervention ownership, deadlines, and capacity-aware execution plan. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Keep interventions realistic given capacity. Prioritize high-value, high-risk accounts with clear save economics.
failure_modes: High-risk accounts lack owners or deadlines.
Interventions exceed available team capacity.
Risk drivers are generic and not evidence-based.
Escalation thresholds are undefined.
follow_up_prompts: Generate customer-specific retention conversation agendas.

Design a weekly churn intervention standup scorecard.

prompts.title: Service Contract Renewal Rescue Plan
prompts.use_case: Recover service contracts at risk of non-renewal through technical and commercial intervention.
prompts.purpose: Preserve aftermarket revenue and installed-base loyalty by converting risk signals into renewal rescue actions.

variables.name: contract_portfolio
variables.description: Contracts due for renewal with account context.
variables.example: 62 contracts renewing in next 120 days

variables.name: renewal_risk_signals
variables.example: Delayed responses, reduced usage, procurement objections

variables.name: service_performance_metrics

variables.name: customer_cost_pressures

variables.name: alternative_vendor_pressure

prompts.expected_output: A renewal rescue plan with risk-ranked contracts, remediation actions, structured concessions, and tracking board design. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Anchor rescue proposals in demonstrated service outcomes, not discounting alone.
failure_modes: High-risk contracts lack clear owner and action date.

Service remediation is not metric-driven.

prompts.purpose: Enable coordinated leadership engagement for strategic account recovery with clear governance and success criteria.

variables.example: Six enterprise accounts previously above 1M annual spend

variables.name: historic_account_value
variables.description: Historical revenue and strategic importance context.

Create re-entry governance meeting agenda template.

prompts.title: Adjacent Market Entry Scorecard
prompts.use_case: Evaluate adjacent markets for IMI expansion with structured attractiveness and fit scoring.
prompts.purpose: Improve expansion decisions by ranking adjacent markets using objective fit, access, and risk dimensions.

variables.name: candidate_markets
variables.description: List of adjacent markets being considered.
variables.example: Battery recycling, packaging automation, aerospace fabrication

variables.name: imi_capability_profile
variables.description: Current IMI technical and operational strengths.
variables.example: Magnetic handling design, custom integration, field service

variables.name: market_demand_signals
variables.description: Demand evidence for each candidate market.
variables.example: RFP volume trends, trade activity, customer inquiry growth

variables.name: competitive_intensity_notes
variables.example: High concentration in packaging, fragmented in battery recycling

variables.name: channel_access_constraints
variables.example: Limited existing channel partnerships in aerospace

variables.name: capacity_limits
variables.example: Applications engineering bandwidth capped at three major launches

prompts.expected_output: A ranked adjacent-market scorecard with go/no-go rationale and candidate-specific entry strategies. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Use explicit tradeoffs rather than optimistic narrative. Deprioritize markets that exceed current execution capacity.
failure_modes: Scoring criteria are inconsistent across markets.
Capacity constraints are ignored in recommendations.
No-go rationale is missing for low-priority markets.
Assumptions are unstated or hidden.
follow_up_prompts: Build a first-year entry execution roadmap for top candidate.
Generate resource demand estimate by function for selected market.
Create a risk mitigation register for market entry execution.

variables.name: current_revenue_by_territory

variables.name: target_industry_density

variables.name: candidate_partner_pool

variables.name: territory_targets

variables.name: capability_requirements

prompts.purpose: Determine whether IMI can enter a target country or region without unacceptable compliance, service, or logistics risk.

variables.name: target_region
variables.description: International region or country under evaluation.
variables.example: Germany and surrounding DACH market

variables.name: product_scope
variables.example: Magnetic separators and lifting systems

variables.name: regulatory_requirements

variables.name: historical_delay_points

prompts.expected_output: A bottleneck-mapped engineering change process with root-cause-linked corrective actions and governance recommendations. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.

prompts.title: Manufacturing Cell Flow Balancing Map
prompts.use_case: Map and rebalance production cell flow to reduce idle time and throughput variability.
prompts.purpose: Increase throughput stability by identifying imbalance between stations, changeovers, and queue accumulation.

variables.name: cell_scope
variables.example: Magnet assembly and final test cell A

variables.name: station_cycle_times
variables.example: Prep 6m, assembly 11m, test 9m, pack 5m

variables.name: takt_target
variables.example: 8 minutes

variables.name: changeover_profile
variables.example: Average 22 minutes, 3 times per shift

variables.name: queue_inventory_levels
variables.description: Current WIP queue levels at station boundaries.
variables.example: High queue before assembly and test

variables.name: labor_skill_constraints
variables.example: Only two operators certified for test station

prompts.expected_output: A flow-balancing process map with quantified station gaps, rebalance options, and throughput KPI plan. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Avoid one-size recommendations. Balance gains should be tied to station-specific constraints and skill realities.
failure_modes: Takt gap analysis is incomplete by station.
Recommendations ignore labor skill constraints.
Queue/WIP dynamics are not addressed.
No implementation sequencing is provided.
follow_up_prompts: Generate a 30-day pilot plan for selected rebalance actions.
Create a cross-training plan to relieve skill bottlenecks.
Draft daily management board metrics for the target cell.

prompts.title: Procurement Lead-Time Value Stream Map
prompts.use_case: Map procurement process for long-lead items and identify leverage points for lead-time compression.
prompts.purpose: Reduce supply risk and schedule slippage by identifying controllable lead-time drivers in procurement workflow.

variables.name: critical_item_set
variables.description: Purchased items with highest schedule impact.
variables.example: Special alloys, coils, custom machined housings

variables.name: supplier_list
variables.example: 8 key suppliers with varying OTD performance

variables.name: sourcing_process_steps
variables.description: Current sourcing and release process stages.
variables.example: Demand signal, RFQ, quote approval, PO release, confirmation

variables.name: approval_and_release_delays
variables.description: Known internal delays before PO placement.
variables.example: Approval queue averages 4 business days

variables.name: supplier_performance_data
variables.description: Historical supplier lead-time and quality performance.
variables.example: OTD ranges 62-93 percent across key suppliers

variables.name: expedite_policy_constraints
variables.description: Limits on expedite options and premium freight.
variables.example: Expedite allowed only for customer-critical jobs over 100k

prompts.expected_output: A procurement value stream map with ranked lead-time drivers and a phased compression action plan. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Focus on controllable leverage points first. Compression should not compromise incoming quality stability.
failure_modes: Internal and supplier delays are not separated.
Actions are proposed without measurable lead-time effects.
Variability drivers are ignored.
Risk controls for quality/cost side effects are missing.
follow_up_prompts: Draft supplier engagement agenda for top delay drivers.
Build internal approval SLA redesign proposal.
Create lead-time compression KPI dashboard for weekly review.

prompts.title: Complaint-to-Corrective Action Process Map
prompts.use_case: Map customer complaint response process through corrective action closure to reduce recurrence.
prompts.purpose: Improve quality response speed and effectiveness by clarifying complaint triage, root-cause, and closure controls.

variables.name: complaint_types
variables.description: Classes of customer complaints under review.
variables.example: Performance shortfall, delivery damage, documentation error

variables.name: current_response_workflow
variables.description: Current process steps from complaint intake to closure.
variables.example: Intake, triage, containment, root-cause, corrective action, verification

variables.name: root_cause_methods_used
variables.description: Methods currently used for root-cause analysis.
variables.example: 5-Why, fishbone, fault tree depending on severity

variables.name: closure_criteria
variables.description: Current criteria required to close complaint cases.
variables.example: Containment complete and customer notified, but verification inconsistent

variables.name: recurrence_data
variables.description: Historical recurrence patterns for complaint classes.
variables.example: 18 percent recurrence in wiring-related complaints

variables.name: customer_communication_rules
variables.description: Communication standards for updates to customer.
variables.example: Initial response in 24h, weekly updates for severe cases

prompts.expected_output: A complaint-to-corrective-action process map with failure points, improved controls, and recurrence-focused KPIs. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: Treat closure as validated prevention, not administrative completion.
failure_modes: Customer communication checkpoints are missing.
Closure criteria are vague or subjective.
Recurrence analysis is not integrated into process improvements.
Failure-point effects are not tied to countermeasures.
follow_up_prompts: Generate standardized closure checklist by complaint severity.
Build escalation protocol for repeat complaints.
Create monthly quality governance dashboard for recurrence.

prompts.expected_output: A standardized installation/commissioning process map with variation logic, prevention checklist, and KPI framework. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.

Variation logic introduces uncontrolled process drift.

Issue prevention lacks linkage to known startup failures.
follow_up_prompts: Create field execution checklist from this process map.

Generate startup issue escalation matrix by severity.

prompts.title: Magnetic Lift Application Fit Assessment
prompts.use_case: Determine technical suitability of magnetic lifting solution for specified customer handling scenario.
prompts.purpose: Reduce misapplication risk by evaluating lifting requirements, constraints, and safety factors before solution selection.

variables.name: material_profile
variables.description: Material type, magnetic properties, and finish conditions.
variables.example: Low-carbon steel sheets with oil film

variables.name: part_geometry
variables.description: Dimensions and shape features affecting lift behavior.
variables.example: 1.2m x 0.8m blanks with stamped openings

variables.name: cycle_requirements
variables.description: Required handling cycle speed and duty cycle.
variables.example: 7-second pick/place at 80 percent duty

variables.name: environmental_conditions
variables.description: Ambient and process conditions impacting performance.
variables.example: Oil mist, 42C ambient, intermittent vibration

variables.name: safety_standard_requirements
variables.example: OSHA handling requirements and internal lockout policy

prompts.expected_output: A technical fit brief with suitability decision, criterion-level scoring, risk mitigations, and validation data gaps. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.
prompts.coaching_notes: When uncertain, recommend conditional fit with targeted validation instead of overconfident suitability claims.
failure_modes: Suitability decision ignores missing safety-critical data.
Assessment does not include criterion-level scoring.
Risks are generic and not tied to application physics.
Validation data gaps are omitted.
follow_up_prompts: Generate a validation test matrix for conditional-fit concerns.
Create a customer-facing technical assumption sheet.
Draft mitigation implementation sequence for top risks.

prompts.title: Separator Configuration Recommendation

prompts.purpose: Improve separator selection quality by aligning configuration decisions with stream behavior and operating constraints.

variables.name: stream_material_profile
variables.description: Composition of material stream being processed.
variables.example: Shredded mixed non-ferrous with fines and occasional ferrous carryover

variables.name: contamination_targets

variables.name: throughput_tph
variables.description: Required throughput in tons per hour.

variables.name: particle_size_distribution

variables.name: available_footprint
variables.example: 4m x 8m including access clearance

variables.name: utility_constraints

prompts.expected_output: A separator configuration recommendation with option comparison, tradeoffs, and commissioning validation checks. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.

Integration constraints are ignored.
Validation checks are missing.

prompts.title: Workholding Design Tradeoff Matrix

prompts.purpose: Improve concept selection by making design tradeoffs explicit before detailed engineering commitment.

variables.name: candidate_concepts
variables.example: Electro-permanent grid, fixed permanent array, hybrid fixture

variables.name: machining_process_requirements

variables.name: part_family_variation

variables.name: precision_and_repeatability_targets

variables.name: maintenance_constraints

variables.name: cost_target

prompts.expected_output: A weighted tradeoff matrix with primary/fallback concept recommendation and pre-freeze validation requirements. Output must be delivered as structured tables or explicitly labeled sections with no blank required fields.

variables.name: motion_profile_constraints

variables.name: control_sequence_notes

variables.name: design_package_summary

variables.example: Magnetic handling system with PLC safety interlocks and guarding

variables.name: applicable_standards

variables.name: hazard_scenarios

variables.name: safeguard_designs
